## Definitions — 7.1. Modifiers {#manual-definitions-71-modifiers}

> 📄 Source: https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Definitions/Modifiers/

Declarations accept a consistent set of *modifiers*, all of which are optional.
Modifiers change some aspect of the declaration's interpretation; for example, they can add documentation or change its scope.
The order of modifiers is fixed, but not every kind of declaration accepts every kind of modifier.

syntaxDeclaration Modifiers

Modifiers consist of the following, in order, all of which are optional:

1. a documentation comment,
2. a list of [attributes](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Attributes/#--tech-term-Attributes),
3. namespace control, specifying whether the resulting name is [private]](#manual---tech-term-private) or [protected]](#manual---tech-term-protected),
4. the `noncomputable` keyword, which exempts a definition from compilation,
5. the `unsafe` keyword, and
6. a recursion modifier `partial` or `nonrec`, which disable termination proofs or disallow recursion entirely.

```lean
declModifiers ::=
    [docComment]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___docComment)?
    [attributes](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Attributes/#Lean___Parser___Term___attributes-next)?
    visibility?
    noncomputable?
    unsafe?
    (partial | nonrec)?
```

*Documentation comments* are used to provide in-source API documentation for the declaration that they modify.
Documentation comments are not, in fact comments: it is a syntax error to put a documentation comment in a position where it is not processed as documentation.
They also occur in positions where some kind of text is required, but string escaping would be onerous, such as the desired messages on the [`#guard_msgs`]](#manual-Lean___guardMsgsCmd) command.

syntaxDocumentation Comments

Documentation comments are like ordinary block comments, but they begin with the sequence `/--` rather than `/-`; just like ordinary comments, they are terminated with `-/`.

```lean
docComment ::=
    /--
    ...
    -/
```

Attributes are an extensible collection of modifiers that associate additional information with declarations.
They are described in a [dedicated section](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Attributes/#attributes).

If a declaration is marked `private`, then it is not accessible outside the module in which it is defined.
If it is `protected`, then opening its namespace does not bring it into scope.

Functions marked `noncomputable` are not compiled and cannot be executed.
Functions must be noncomputable if they use noncomputable reasoning principles such as the axiom of choice or excluded middle to produce data that is relevant to the answer that they return, or if they use features of Lean that are exempted from code generation for efficiency reasons, such as [recursors]](#manual---tech-term-recursor).
Noncomputable functions are very useful for specification and reasoning, even if they cannot be compiled and executed.

The `unsafe` marker exempts a definition from kernel checking and enables it to access features that may undermine Lean's guarantees.
It should be used with great care, and only with a thorough understanding of Lean's internals.

---



## Definitions — 7.2. Headers and Signatures {#manual-definitions-72-headers-and-signatures}

> 📄 Source: https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Definitions/Headers-and-Signatures/

The *header* of a definition or declaration consists of the constant being declared or defined, if relevant, together with its signature.
The *signature* of a constant specifies how it can be used.
The information present in the signature is more than just the type, including information such as [universe level parameters]](#manual---tech-term-universe-parameters) and the default values of its optional parameters.
In Lean, signatures are written in a consistent format in different kinds of declarations.

### 7.2.1. Declaration Names {#manual-The-Lean-Language-Reference--Definitions--Headers-and-Signatures--Declaration-Names}

Most headers begin with a *declaration name*, which is followed by the signature proper: its parameters and the resulting type.
A declaration name is a name that may optionally include universe parameters.

syntaxDeclaration Names

Declaration names without universe parameters consist of an identifier:

```lean
declId ::=
    ident
```

Declaration names with universe parameters consist of an identifier followed by a period and one or more universe parameter names in braces:

```lean
declId ::= ...
    | ident.{ident, ident,*}
```

These universe parameter names are binding occurrences.

Examples do not include declaration names, and names are optional for instance declarations.

### 7.2.2. Parameters and Types {#manual-parameter-syntax}

After the name, if present, is the header's signature.
The signature specifies the declaration's parameters and type.

syntaxDeclaration Signatures

A signature consists of zero or more parameters, followed by a colon and a type.

```lean
declSig ::=
    (ident | [hole](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Terms/Holes/#Lean___Parser___Term___hole) | bracketedBinder)* : term
```

syntaxOptional Signatures

Signatures are often optional.
In these cases, parameters may be supplied even if the type is omitted.

```lean
optDeclSig ::=
    (ident | [hole](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Terms/Holes/#Lean___Parser___Term___hole) | bracketedBinder)* (: term)?
```

Parameters may have three forms:

- An identifier, which names a parameter but does not provide a type.
  These parameters' types must be inferred during elaboration.
- An underscore (`_`), which indicates a parameter that is not accessible by name in the local scope.
  These parameters' types must also be inferred during elaboration.
- A bracketed binder, which may specify every aspect of one or more parameters, including their names, their types, default values, and whether they are explicit, implicit, strictly implicit, or instance-implicit.

### 7.2.3. Bracketed Parameter Bindings {#manual-bracketed-parameter-syntax}

Parameters other than identifiers or underscores are collectively referred to as *bracketed binders* because every syntactic form for specifying them has some kind of brackets, braces, or parentheses.
All bracketed binders specify the type of a parameter, and most include parameter names.
The name is optional for instance implicit parameters.
Using an underscore (`_`) instead of a parameter name indicates an anonymous parameter.

syntaxExplicit Parameters

Parenthesized parameters indicate explicit parameters.
If more than one identifier or underscore is provided, then all of them become parameters with the same type.

```lean
bracketedBinder ::=
    ((ident | [hole](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Terms/Holes/#Lean___Parser___Term___hole)) (ident | [hole](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Terms/Holes/#Lean___Parser___Term___hole))* : term)
```

syntaxOptional and Automatic Parameters

Parenthesized parameters with a `:=` assign default values to parameters.
Parameters with default values are called *optional parameters*.
At a call site, if the parameter is not provided, then the provided term is used to fill it in.
Prior parameters in the signature are in scope for the default value, and their values at the call site are substituted into the default value term.

If a [tactic script](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Tactic-Proofs/#tactics) is provided, then the tactics are executed at the call site to synthesize a parameter value; parameters that are filled in via tactics are called *automatic parameters*.

```lean
bracketedBinder ::= ...
    | ((ident | [hole](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Terms/Holes/#Lean___Parser___Term___hole)) (ident | [hole](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Terms/Holes/#Lean___Parser___Term___hole))* : term := term)
```

syntaxImplicit Parameters

Parameters in curly braces indicate [implicit](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Terms/Functions/#--tech-term-implicit) parameters.
Unless provided by name at a call site, these parameters are expected to be synthesized via unification at call sites.
Implicit parameters are synthesized at all call sites.

```lean
bracketedBinder ::= ...
    | {(ident | [hole](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Terms/Holes/#Lean___Parser___Term___hole)) (ident | [hole](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Terms/Holes/#Lean___Parser___Term___hole))* : term}
```

syntaxStrict Implicit Parameters

Parameters in double curly braces indicate [strict implicit](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Terms/Functions/#--tech-term-Strict-implicit) parameters.
`⦃ … ⦄` and `{{ … }}` are equivalent.
Like implicit parameters, these parameters are expected to be synthesized via unification at call sites when they are not provided by name.
Strict implicit parameters are only synthesized at call sites when subsequent parameters in the signature are also provided.

```lean
bracketedBinder ::= ...
    | ⦃(ident | [hole](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Terms/Holes/#Lean___Parser___Term___hole)) (ident | [hole](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Terms/Holes/#Lean___Parser___Term___hole))* : term⦄
```

```lean
bracketedBinder ::= ...
    | {{(ident | [hole](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Terms/Holes/#Lean___Parser___Term___hole)) (ident | [hole](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Terms/Holes/#Lean___Parser___Term___hole))* : term}}
```

syntaxInstance Implicit Parameters

Parameters in square brackets indicate [instance implicit](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Type-Classes/#--tech-term-instance-implicit) parameters, which are synthesized at call sites using [instance synthesis](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Type-Classes/#--tech-term-synthesizes).

```lean
bracketedBinder ::= ...
    | [(ident :)? term]
```

The parameters are always in scope in the signature's type, which occurs after the colon.
They are also in scope in the declaration's body, while names bound in the type itself are only in scope in the type.
Thus, parameter names are used twice:

- As names in the declaration's function type, bound as part of a [dependent function type]](#manual---tech-term-Dependent).
- As names in the declaration's body.
  In function definitions, they are bound by a `fun`.

**Example: Parameter Scope**

The signature of `[add]](#manual-add-_LPAR_in-Parameter-Scope_RPAR_)` contains one parameter, `n`.
Additionally, the signature's type is `(k : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)) → [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)`, which is a function type that includes `k`.
The parameter `n` is in scope in the function's body, but `k` is not.

```lean
def add (n : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)) : (k : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)) → [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)
| 0 => n
| k' + 1 => 1 + [add]](#manual-add-_LPAR_in-Parameter-Scope_RPAR_) n k'
```

Like `[add]](#manual-add-_LPAR_in-Parameter-Scope_RPAR_)`, the signature of `[mustBeEqual]](#manual-mustBeEqual-_LPAR_in-Parameter-Scope_RPAR_)` contains one parameter, `n`.
It is in scope both in the type, where it occurs in a proposition, and in the body, where it occurs as part of the message.

```lean
def mustBeEqual (n : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)) : (k : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)) → n = k → [String](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Strings/#String___ofByteArray) :=
fun _ =>
fun
| [rfl](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#rfl-next) => s!"Equal - both are {n}!"
```

The section on [function application](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Terms/Function-Application/#function-application) describes the interpretation of [optional]](#manual---tech-term-optional-parameters), [automatic]](#manual---tech-term-automatic-parameters), [implicit](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Terms/Functions/#--tech-term-implicit), and [instance implicit](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Type-Classes/#--tech-term-instance-implicit) parameters in detail.

### 7.2.4. Automatic Implicit Parameters {#manual-automatic-implicit-parameters}

By default, otherwise-unbound names that occur in signatures are converted into implicit parameters when possible
These parameters are called *automatic implicit parameters*.
This is possible when they are not in the function position of an application and when there is sufficient information available in the signature to infer their type and any ordering constraints on them.
This process is iterated: if the inferred type for the freshly-inserted implicit parameter has dependencies that are not uniquely determined, then these dependencies are replaced with further implicit parameters.

Implicit parameters that don't correspond to names written in signatures are assigned names akin to those of [inaccessible](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Tactic-Proofs/Reading-Proof-States/#--tech-term-inaccessible) hypotheses in proofs, which cannot be referred to.
They show up in signatures with a trailing dagger (`'✝'`).
This prevents an arbitrary choice of name by Lean from becoming part of the API by being usable as a [named argument](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Terms/Function-Application/#--tech-term-named-arguments).

**Example: Automatic Implicit Parameters**

In this definition of `[map]](#manual-map-_LPAR_in-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_)`, `α` and `β` are not explicitly bound.
Rather than this being an error, they are converted into implicit parameters.
Because they must be types, but nothing constrains their universes, the universe parameters `u` and `v` are also inserted.

```lean
def map (f : α → β) : (xs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) α) → [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) β
| [] => []
| x :: xs => f x :: [map]](#manual-map-_LPAR_in-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) f xs
```

The full signature of `[map]](#manual-map-_LPAR_in-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_)` is:

```lean
[map]](#manual-map-_LPAR_in-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_).{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v}
(f : α → β) (xs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) α) :
[List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) β
```

**Example: No Automatic Implicit Parameters**

In this definition, `α` and `β` are not explicitly bound.
Because `[autoImplicit]](#manual-autoImplicit)` is disabled, this is an error:

```lean
set_option [autoImplicit]](#manual-autoImplicit) false
def map (f : α → β) : (xs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) α) → [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) β
| [] => []
| x :: xs => f x :: map f xs
```

```lean
Unknown identifier `α`

Note: It is not possible to treat `α` as an implicitly bound variable here because the `autoImplicit` option is set to `[false](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Booleans/#Bool___false)`.
```

```lean
Unknown identifier `β`

Note: It is not possible to treat `β` as an implicitly bound variable here because the `autoImplicit` option is set to `[false](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Booleans/#Bool___false)`.
```

The full signature allows the definition to be accepted:

```lean
set_option [autoImplicit]](#manual-autoImplicit) false
def map.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v}
(f : α → β) :
(xs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) α) → [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) β
| [] => []
| x :: xs => f x :: map f xs
```

Universe parameters are inserted automatically for parameters without explicit type annotations.
The type parameters' universes can be inferred, and the appropriate universe parameters inserted, even when `[autoImplicit]](#manual-autoImplicit)` is disabled:

```lean
set_option [autoImplicit]](#manual-autoImplicit) false
def map {α β} (f : α → β) :
(xs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) α) → [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) β
| [] => []
| x :: xs => f x :: map f xs
```

**Example: Iterated Automatic Implicit Parameters**

Given a number bounded by `n`, represented by the type `Fin n`, an `[AtLeast]](#manual-AtLeast-_LPAR_in-Iterated-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) i` is a natural number paired with a proof that it is at least as large as `i`.

```lean
structure AtLeast (i : [Fin](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Finite-Natural-Numbers/#Fin___mk) n) where
val : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)
val_gt_i : val ≥ i.[val](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Finite-Natural-Numbers/#Fin___mk)
```

These numbers can be added:

```lean
def AtLeast.add (x y : [AtLeast]](#manual-AtLeast-_LPAR_in-Iterated-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) i) : [AtLeast]](#manual-AtLeast-_LPAR_in-Iterated-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) i :=
AtLeast.mk (x.[val]](#manual-AtLeast___val-_LPAR_in-Iterated-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) + y.[val]](#manual-AtLeast___val-_LPAR_in-Iterated-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_)) <| byn✝:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)i:[Fin](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Finite-Natural-Numbers/#Fin___mk) n✝x:[AtLeast]](#manual-AtLeast-_LPAR_in-Iterated-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) iy:[AtLeast]](#manual-AtLeast-_LPAR_in-Iterated-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) i⊢ x.[val]](#manual-AtLeast___val-_LPAR_in-Iterated-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) [+](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk) y.[val]](#manual-AtLeast___val-_LPAR_in-Iterated-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) ≥ ↑i
[cases](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#cases) xmkn✝:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)i:[Fin](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Finite-Natural-Numbers/#Fin___mk) n✝y:[AtLeast]](#manual-AtLeast-_LPAR_in-Iterated-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) ival✝:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)val_gt_i✝:val✝ ≥ ↑i⊢ { [val]](#manual-AtLeast___val-_LPAR_in-Iterated-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) := val✝, [val_gt_i]](#manual-AtLeast___val_gt_i-_LPAR_in-Iterated-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) := val_gt_i✝ }.[val]](#manual-AtLeast___val-_LPAR_in-Iterated-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) [+](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk) y.[val]](#manual-AtLeast___val-_LPAR_in-Iterated-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) ≥ ↑i
[cases](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#cases) ymk.mkn✝:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)i:[Fin](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Finite-Natural-Numbers/#Fin___mk) n✝val✝¹:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)val_gt_i✝¹:val✝ ≥ ↑ival✝:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)val_gt_i✝:val✝ ≥ ↑i⊢ { [val]](#manual-AtLeast___val-_LPAR_in-Iterated-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) := val✝¹, [val_gt_i]](#manual-AtLeast___val_gt_i-_LPAR_in-Iterated-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) := val_gt_i✝¹ }.[val]](#manual-AtLeast___val-_LPAR_in-Iterated-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) [+](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk) { [val]](#manual-AtLeast___val-_LPAR_in-Iterated-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) := val✝, [val_gt_i]](#manual-AtLeast___val_gt_i-_LPAR_in-Iterated-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) := val_gt_i✝ }.[val]](#manual-AtLeast___val-_LPAR_in-Iterated-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) ≥ ↑i
[dsimp](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#dsimp) [only](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#dsimp)mk.mkn✝:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)i:[Fin](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Finite-Natural-Numbers/#Fin___mk) n✝val✝¹:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)val_gt_i✝¹:val✝ ≥ ↑ival✝:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)val_gt_i✝:val✝ ≥ ↑i⊢ val✝¹ [+](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#HAdd___mk) val✝ ≥ ↑i
[omega](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#omega)All goals completed! 🐙
```

The signature of `[AtLeast.add]](#manual-AtLeast___add-_LPAR_in-Iterated-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_)` requires multiple rounds of automatic implicit parameter insertion.
First, `i` is inserted; but its type depends on the upper bound `n` of `[Fin](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Finite-Natural-Numbers/#Fin___mk) n`.
In the second round, `n` is inserted, using a machine-chosen name.
Because `n`'s type is `[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)`, which has no dependencies, the process terminates.
The final signature can be seen with [`#check`]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___check):

```lean
[#check]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___check) [AtLeast.add]](#manual-AtLeast___add-_LPAR_in-Iterated-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_)
```

```lean
[AtLeast.add]](#manual-AtLeast___add-_LPAR_in-Iterated-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) {n✝ : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)} {i : [Fin](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Finite-Natural-Numbers/#Fin___mk) n✝} (x y : [AtLeast]](#manual-AtLeast-_LPAR_in-Iterated-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) i) : [AtLeast]](#manual-AtLeast-_LPAR_in-Iterated-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) i
```

Automatic implicit parameter insertion takes place after the insertion of parameters due to [section variables]](#manual---tech-term-Section-variables).
Parameters that correspond to section variables have the same name as the corresponding variable, even when they do not correspond to a name written directly in the signature, and disabling automatic implicit parameters has no effect the parameters that correspond to section variables.
However, when automatic implicit parameters are enabled, section variable declarations that contain otherwise-unbound variables receive additional section variables that follow the same rules as those for implicit parameters.

Automatic implicit parameters insertion is controlled by two options.
By default, automatic implicit parameter insertion is *relaxed*, which means that any unbound identifier may be a candidate for automatic insertion.
Setting the option `[relaxedAutoImplicit]](#manual-relaxedAutoImplicit)` to `[false](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Booleans/#Bool___false)` disables relaxed mode and causes only identifiers that consist of a single character followed by zero or more digits to be considered for automatic insertion.

option

```lean
relaxedAutoImplicit
```

Default value: `[true](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Booleans/#Bool___false)`

When "relaxed" mode is enabled, any atomic nonempty identifier is eligible for auto bound implicit locals (see option `[autoImplicit]](#manual-autoImplicit)`).

option

```lean
autoImplicit
```

Default value: `[true](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Booleans/#Bool___false)`

Unbound local variables in declaration headers become implicit arguments. In "relaxed" mode (default), any atomic identifier is eligible, otherwise only single character followed by numeric digits are eligible. For example, `def f (x : Vector α n) : Vector α n :=` automatically introduces the implicit variables {α n}.

**Example: Relaxed vs Non-Relaxed Automatic Implicit Parameters**

Misspelled identifiers or missing imports can end up as unwanted implicit parameters, as in this example:

```lean
inductive Answer where
| yes
| maybe
| no
```

```lean
def select (choices : α × α × α) : Asnwer → α
| .yes => choices.1
| .maybe => choices.2.1
| .no => choices.2.2
```

The resulting error message states that the argument's type is not a constant, so dot notation cannot be used in the pattern:

```lean
Invalid dotted identifier notation: The expected type of `.yes`
  Asnwer
is not of the form `C ...` or `... → C ...` where C is a constant
```

This is because the signature is:

```lean
select.{u_1, u_2}
{α : Type u_1}
{Asnwer : Sort u_2}
(choices : α × α × α) :
Asnwer → α
```

Disabling relaxed automatic implicit parameters makes the error more clear, while still allowing the type to be inserted automatically:

```lean
set_option [relaxedAutoImplicit]](#manual-relaxedAutoImplicit) false
def select (choices : α × α × α) : Asnwer → α
| .yes => choices.1
| .maybe => choices.2.1
| .no => choices.2.2
```

```lean
Unknown identifier `Asnwer`

Note: It is not possible to treat `Asnwer` as an implicitly bound variable here because it has multiple characters while the `relaxedAutoImplicit` option is set to `[false](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Booleans/#Bool___false)`.
```

Correcting the error allows the definition to be accepted.

```lean
set_option [relaxedAutoImplicit]](#manual-relaxedAutoImplicit) false
def select (choices : α × α × α) : [Answer]](#manual-Answer-_LPAR_in-Relaxed-vs-Non-Relaxed-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) → α
| [.yes]](#manual-Answer___yes-_LPAR_in-Relaxed-vs-Non-Relaxed-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) => choices.[1](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Tuples/#Prod___mk)
| [.maybe]](#manual-Answer___maybe-_LPAR_in-Relaxed-vs-Non-Relaxed-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) => choices.[2](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Tuples/#Prod___mk).[1](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Tuples/#Prod___mk)
| [.no]](#manual-Answer___no-_LPAR_in-Relaxed-vs-Non-Relaxed-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) => choices.[2](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Tuples/#Prod___mk).[2](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Tuples/#Prod___mk)
```

Turning off automatic implicit parameters entirely leads to the definition being rejected:

```lean
set_option [autoImplicit]](#manual-autoImplicit) false
def select (choices : α × α × α) : [Answer]](#manual-Answer-_LPAR_in-Relaxed-vs-Non-Relaxed-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) → α
| [.yes]](#manual-Answer___yes-_LPAR_in-Relaxed-vs-Non-Relaxed-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) => choices.[1](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Tuples/#Prod___mk)
| [.maybe]](#manual-Answer___maybe-_LPAR_in-Relaxed-vs-Non-Relaxed-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) => choices.[2](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Tuples/#Prod___mk).[1](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Tuples/#Prod___mk)
| [.no]](#manual-Answer___no-_LPAR_in-Relaxed-vs-Non-Relaxed-Automatic-Implicit-Parameters_RPAR_) => choices.[2](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Tuples/#Prod___mk).[2](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Tuples/#Prod___mk)
```

```lean
Unknown identifier `α`

Note: It is not possible to treat `α` as an implicitly bound variable here because the `autoImplicit` option is set to `[false](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Booleans/#Bool___false)`.
```

## Definitions — 7.3. Definitions {#manual-definitions-73-definitions}

> 📄 Source: https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Definitions/Definitions/

Definitions add a new constant to the global environment as a name that stands for a term.
As part of the kernel's definitional equality, this new constant may be replaced via [δ-reduction]](#manual---tech-term-___-next) with the term that it stands for.
In the elaborator, this replacement is governed by the constant's [reducibility](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Definitions/Recursive-Definitions/#--tech-term-reducibility).
The new constant may be [universe polymorphic]](#manual---tech-term-universe-polymorphism), in which case occurrences may instantiate it with different universe level parameters.

Function definitions may be recursive.
To preserve the consistency of Lean's type theory as a logic, recursive functions must either be opaque to the kernel (e.g. by [declaring them `partial`](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Definitions/Recursive-Definitions/#partial-functions)) or proven to terminate with one of the strategies described in [the section on recursive definitions](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Definitions/Recursive-Definitions/#recursive-definitions).

The headers and bodies of definitions are elaborated together.
If the header is incompletely specified (e.g. a parameter's type or the codomain is missing), then the body may provide sufficient information for the elaborator to reconstruct the missing parts.
However, [instance implicit](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Type-Classes/#--tech-term-instance-implicit) parameters must be specified in the header or as [section variables]](#manual---tech-term-Section-variables).

syntaxDefinitions

Definitions that use `:=` associate the term on the right-hand side with the constant's name.
The term is wrapped in a `fun` for each parameter, and the type is found by binding the parameters in a function type.
Definitions with `def` are [semireducible](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Definitions/Recursive-Definitions/#--tech-term-Semireducible).

```lean
command ::= ...
    | [declModifiers]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___declModifiers)
      def declId [optDeclSig]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___optDeclSig) := term
```

Definitions may use pattern matching.
These definitions are desugared to uses of [`match`](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Terms/Pattern-Matching/#Lean___Parser___Term___match).

```lean
command ::= ...
    | [declModifiers]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___declModifiers)
      def declId [optDeclSig]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___optDeclSig)
        (| term => term)*
```

Values of structure types, or functions that return them, may be defined by providing values for their fields, following `where`:

```lean
command ::= ...
    | [declModifiers]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___declModifiers)
      def declId [optDeclSig]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___optDeclSig) where
        structInstField*
```

In [modules]](#manual---tech-term-module), the bodies of definitions defined with `def` are not exposed by default.

syntaxAbbreviations

Abbreviations are identical to definitions with `def`, except they are [reducible](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Definitions/Recursive-Definitions/#--tech-term-Reducible).

```lean
command ::= ...
    | [declModifiers]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___declModifiers)
      abbrev declId [optDeclSig]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___optDeclSig) := term
```

```lean
command ::= ...
    | [declModifiers]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___declModifiers)
      abbrev declId [optDeclSig]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___optDeclSig)
        (| term => term)*
```

```lean
command ::= ...
    | [declModifiers]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___declModifiers)
      abbrev declId [optDeclSig]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___optDeclSig) where
        structInstField*
```

In [modules]](#manual---tech-term-module), the bodies of definitions defined with `abbrev` are exposed by default.

*Opaque constants* are defined constants that are not subject to [δ-reduction]](#manual---tech-term-___-next) in the kernel.
They are useful for specifying the existence of some function.
Unlike [axioms](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Axioms/#--tech-term-Axioms), opaque declarations can only be used for types that are inhabited, so they do not risk introducing inconsistency.
Also unlike axioms, the inhabitant of the type is used in compiled code.
The `implemented_by` attribute can be used to instruct the compiler to emit a call to some other function as the compilation of an opaque constant.

syntaxOpaque Constants

Opaque definitions with right-hand sides are elaborated like other definitions.
This demonstrates that the type is inhabited; the inhabitant plays no further role.

```lean
command ::= ...
    | [declModifiers]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___declModifiers)
      opaque declId [declSig]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___declSig) := term
```

Opaque constants may also be specified without right-hand sides.
The elaborator fills in the right-hand side by synthesizing an instance of `[Inhabited](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#Inhabited___mk)`, or `[Nonempty](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Type-Classes/Basic-Classes/#Nonempty___intro)` if that fails.

```lean
command ::= ...
    | [declModifiers]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___declModifiers)
      opaque declId [declSig]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___declSig)
```

---



## Definitions — 7.4. Theorems {#manual-definitions-74-theorems}

> 📄 Source: https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Definitions/Theorems/

Because [propositions]](#manual---tech-term-Propositions) are types whose inhabitants count as proofs, theorems and definitions are technically very similar.
However, because their use cases are quite different, they differ in many details:

- The theorem statement must be a proposition.
  The types of definitions may inhabit any [universe]](#manual---tech-term-universes).
- A theorem's header (that is, the theorem statement) is completely elaborated before the body is elaborated.
  Section variables only become parameters to the theorem if they (or their dependents) are mentioned in the header.
  This prevents changes to a proof from unintentionally changing the theorem statement.
- Theorems are [irreducible](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Definitions/Recursive-Definitions/#--tech-term-Irreducible) by default.
  Because all proofs of the same proposition are [definitionally equal]](#manual---tech-term-definitional-equality), there are few reasons to unfold a theorem.

Theorems may be recursive, subject to the same conditions as [recursive function definitions](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Definitions/Recursive-Definitions/#recursive-definitions).
However, it is more common to use tactics such as `[induction](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#induction)` or `[fun_induction](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#fun_induction)` instead.

syntaxTheorems

The syntax of theorems is like that of definitions, except the codomain (that is, the theorem statement) in the signature is mandatory.

```lean
command ::= ...
    | [declModifiers]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___declModifiers)
      theorem declId [declSig]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___declSig) := term
```

```lean
command ::= ...
    | [declModifiers]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___declModifiers)
      theorem declId [declSig]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___declSig)
        (| term => term)*
```

```lean
command ::= ...
    | [declModifiers]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___declModifiers)
      theorem declId [declSig]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___declSig) where
        structInstField*
```

In [modules]](#manual---tech-term-module), proofs of theorems are not exposed by default.

---



## Definitions — 7.5. Example Declarations {#manual-definitions-75-example-declarations}

> 📄 Source: https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Definitions/Example-Declarations/

An example is an anonymous definition that is elaborated and then discarded.
Examples are useful for incremental testing during development and to make it easier to understand a file.

syntaxExamples

```lean
command ::= ...
    | [declModifiers]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___declModifiers)
      example [optDeclSig]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___optDeclSig) := term
```

```lean
command ::= ...
    | [declModifiers]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___declModifiers)
      example [optDeclSig]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___optDeclSig)
        (| term => term)*
```

```lean
command ::= ...
    | [declModifiers]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___declModifiers)
      example [optDeclSig]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___optDeclSig) where
        structInstField*
```
