```lean
coe : α → β
```

Coerces a value of type `α` to type `β`. Accessible by the notation `↑x`,
or by double type ascription `((x : α) : β)`.

type class

```lean
[CoeTail.{u, v}]](#manual-CoeTail___mk) (α : [semiOutParam]](#manual-semiOutParam) (Sort u)) (β : Sort v) :
  Sort (max (max 1 u) v)



[CoeTail.{u, v}]](#manual-CoeTail___mk) (α : [semiOutParam]](#manual-semiOutParam) (Sort u))
  (β : Sort v) : Sort (max (max 1 u) v)
```

`[CoeTail]](#manual-CoeTail___mk) α β` is for coercions that can only appear at the end of a
sequence of coercions. That is, `α` can be further coerced via `[Coe]](#manual-Coe___mk) σ α` and
`[CoeHead]](#manual-CoeHead___mk) τ σ` instances but `β` will only be the expected type of the expression.

Instance Constructor

```lean
[CoeTail.mk]](#manual-CoeTail___mk).{u, v}
```

Methods

```lean
coe : α → β
```

Coerces a value of type `α` to type `β`. Accessible by the notation `↑x`,
or by double type ascription `((x : α) : β)`.

Instances of `[CoeT]](#manual-CoeT___mk)` can be synthesized when an appropriate chain of instances exists, or when there is a single applicable `[CoeDep]](#manual-CoeDep___mk)` instance.When coercing from `[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)` to another type, a `[NatCast]](#manual-NatCast___mk)` instances also suffices.
If both exist, then the `[CoeDep]](#manual-CoeDep___mk)` instance takes priority.

type class

```lean
[CoeT.{u, v}]](#manual-CoeT___mk) (α : Sort u) : α → (β : Sort v) → Sort (max 1 v)



[CoeT.{u, v}]](#manual-CoeT___mk) (α : Sort u) :
  α → (β : Sort v) → Sort (max 1 v)
```

`[CoeT]](#manual-CoeT___mk)` is the core typeclass which is invoked by Lean to resolve a type error.
It can also be triggered explicitly with the notation `↑x` or by double type
ascription `((x : α) : β)`.

A `[CoeT]](#manual-CoeT___mk)` chain has the grammar `CoeHead? CoeOut* Coe* CoeTail? | CoeDep`.

Instance Constructor

```lean
[CoeT.mk]](#manual-CoeT___mk).{u, v}
```

Methods

```lean
coe : β
```

The resulting value of type `β`. The input `x : α` is a parameter to
the type class, so the value of type `β` may possibly depend on additional
typeclasses on `x`.

Dependent coercions may not be chained.
As an alternative to a chain of coercions, a term `e` of type `α` can be coerced to `β` using an instance of `[CoeDep]](#manual-CoeDep___mk) α e β`.
Dependent coercions are useful in situations where only some of the values can be coerced; this mechanism is used to coerce only decidable propositions to `[Bool](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Booleans/#Bool___false)`.
They are also useful when the value itself occurs in the coercion's target type.

type class

```lean
[CoeDep.{u, v}]](#manual-CoeDep___mk) (α : Sort u) : α → (β : Sort v) → Sort (max 1 v)



[CoeDep.{u, v}]](#manual-CoeDep___mk) (α : Sort u) :
  α → (β : Sort v) → Sort (max 1 v)
```

`[CoeDep]](#manual-CoeDep___mk) α (x : α) β` is a typeclass for dependent coercions, that is, the type `β`
can depend on `x` (or rather, the value of `x` is available to typeclass search
so an instance that relates `β` to `x` is allowed).

Dependent coercions do not participate in the transitive chaining process of
regular coercions: they must exactly match the type mismatch on both sides.

Instance Constructor

```lean
[CoeDep.mk]](#manual-CoeDep___mk).{u, v}
```

Methods

```lean
coe : β
```

The resulting value of type `β`. The input `x : α` is a parameter to
the type class, so the value of type `β` may possibly depend on additional
typeclasses on `x`.

**Example: Dependent Coercion**

A type of non-empty lists can be defined as a pair of a list and a proof that it is not empty.
This type can be coerced to ordinary lists by applying the projection:

```lean
structure NonEmptyList (α : Type u) : Type u where
contents : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) α
non_empty : contents ≠ []
instance : [Coe]](#manual-Coe___mk) ([NonEmptyList]](#manual-NonEmptyList-_LPAR_in-Dependent-Coercion_RPAR_) α) ([List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) α) where
[coe]](#manual-Coe___mk) xs := xs.[contents]](#manual-NonEmptyList___contents-_LPAR_in-Dependent-Coercion_RPAR_)
```

The coercion works as expected:

```lean
def oneTwoThree : [NonEmptyList]](#manual-NonEmptyList-_LPAR_in-Dependent-Coercion_RPAR_) [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) := ⟨[1, 2, 3], by⊢ [[](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil)1[,](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) 2[,](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) 3[]](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) ≠ [[](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil)[]](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) [simp](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#simp)All goals completed! 🐙⟩
[#eval]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___eval) ([oneTwoThree]](#manual-oneTwoThree-_LPAR_in-Dependent-Coercion_RPAR_) : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)) ++ [4]
```

Arbitrary lists cannot, however, be coerced to non-empty lists, because some arbitrarily-chosen lists may indeed be empty:

```lean
instance : [Coe]](#manual-Coe___mk) ([List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) α) ([NonEmptyList]](#manual-NonEmptyList-_LPAR_in-Dependent-Coercion_RPAR_) α) where
[coe]](#manual-Coe___mk) xs := ⟨xs, _⟩
```

```lean
don't know how to synthesize placeholder for argument `non_empty`
context:
α:Type u_1xs:[List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) α⊢ xs ≠ [[](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil)[]](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil)
```

A dependent coercion can restrict the domain of the coercion to only lists that are not empty:

```lean
instance : [CoeDep]](#manual-CoeDep___mk) ([List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) α) (x :: xs) ([NonEmptyList]](#manual-NonEmptyList-_LPAR_in-Dependent-Coercion_RPAR_) α) where
[coe]](#manual-CoeDep___mk) := ⟨x :: xs, byα:Type ?u.7x:αxs:[List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) α⊢ x [::](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) xs ≠ [[](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil)[]](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) [simp](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#simp)All goals completed! 🐙⟩
[#eval]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___eval) ([1, 2, 3] : [NonEmptyList]](#manual-NonEmptyList-_LPAR_in-Dependent-Coercion_RPAR_) [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero))
```

```lean
{ contents := [1, 2, 3], non_empty := _ }
```

Dependent coercion insertion requires that the term to be coerced syntactically matches the term in the instance header.
Lists that are known to be non-empty, but which are not syntactically instances of `(· :: ·)`, cannot be coerced with this instance.

```lean
[#check]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___check)
fun (xs : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)) =>
let ys : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) := xs ++ [4]
(ys : [NonEmptyList]](#manual-NonEmptyList-_LPAR_in-Dependent-Coercion_RPAR_) [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero))
```

When coercion insertion fails, the original type error is reported:

```lean
Type mismatch
  ys
has type
  [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)
but is expected to have type
  [NonEmptyList]](#manual-NonEmptyList-_LPAR_in-Dependent-Coercion_RPAR_) [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)
```

syntaxCoercions

```lean
term ::= ...
    | ↑term
```

Coercions can be explicitly placed using the prefix operator [`↑`]](#manual-coeNotation).

Unlike using nested [type ascriptions](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Terms/Type-Ascription/#--tech-term-Type-ascriptions), the [`↑`]](#manual-coeNotation) syntax for placing coercions does not require the involved types to be written explicitly.

**Example: Controlling Coercion Insertion**

Instance synthesis and coercion insertion interact with one another.
Synthesizing an instance may make type information known that later triggers coercion insertion.
The specific placement of coercions may matter.

In this definition of `[sub]](#manual-sub-_LPAR_in-Controlling-Coercion-Insertion_RPAR_)`, the `[Sub]](#manual-Sub___mk) [Int](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Integers/#Int___ofNat)` instance is synthesized based on the function's return type.
This instance requires that the two parameters also be `[Int](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Integers/#Int___ofNat)`s, but they are `[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)`s.
Coercions are inserted around each argument to the subtraction operator.
This can be seen in the output of `#print`.

```lean
def sub (n k : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)) : [Int](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Integers/#Int___ofNat) := n - k
#print [sub]](#manual-sub-_LPAR_in-Controlling-Coercion-Insertion_RPAR_)
```

```lean
def sub : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → [Int](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Integers/#Int___ofNat) :=
fun n k => ↑n [-]](#manual-HSub___mk) ↑k
```

Placing the coercion operator outside the subtraction causes the elaborator to attempt to infer a type for the subtraction and then insert a coercion.
Because the arguments are both `[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)`s, the `[Sub]](#manual-Sub___mk) [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)` instance is selected, leading to the difference being a `[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)`.
The difference is then coerced to an `[Int](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Integers/#Int___ofNat)`.

```lean
def sub' (n k : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)) : [Int](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Integers/#Int___ofNat) := ↑ (n - k)
#print [sub']](#manual-sub___-_LPAR_in-Controlling-Coercion-Insertion_RPAR_)
```

These two functions are not equivalent because subtraction of natural numbers truncates at zero:

```lean
[#eval]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___eval) [sub]](#manual-sub-_LPAR_in-Controlling-Coercion-Insertion_RPAR_) 4 8
```

```lean
-4
```

```lean
[#eval]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___eval) [sub']](#manual-sub___-_LPAR_in-Controlling-Coercion-Insertion_RPAR_) 4 8
```

```lean
0
```

### 11.2.1. Implementing Coercions {#manual-coercion-impl}

The appropriate `[CoeHead]](#manual-CoeHead___mk)`, `[CoeOut]](#manual-CoeOut___mk)`, `[Coe]](#manual-Coe___mk)`, or `[CoeTail]](#manual-CoeTail___mk)` instance is sufficient to cause a desired coercion to be inserted.
However, the implementation of the coercion should be registered as a coercion using the `coe` attribute.
This causes Lean to display uses of the coercion with the [`↑`]](#manual-coeNotation) operator.
It also causes the `[norm_cast](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#norm_cast)` tactic to treat the coercion as a cast, rather than as an ordinary function.

attributeCoercion Declarations

```lean
attr ::= ...
    | coe
```

The `@[coe]` attribute on a function (which should also appear in a
`instance : Coe A B := ⟨myFn⟩` declaration) allows the delaborator to show
applications of this function as `↑` when printing expressions.

**Example: Implementing Coercions**

The [enum inductive]](#manual---tech-term-enum-inductive) type `[Weekday]](#manual-Weekday-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_)` represents the days of the week:

```lean
inductive Weekday where
| mo | tu | we | th | fr | sa | su
```

As a seven-element type, it contains the same information as `[Fin](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Finite-Natural-Numbers/#Fin___mk) 7`.
There is a bijection:

```lean
def Weekday.toFin : [Weekday]](#manual-Weekday-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_) → [Fin](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Finite-Natural-Numbers/#Fin___mk) 7
| [mo]](#manual-Weekday___mo-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_) => 0
| [tu]](#manual-Weekday___tu-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_) => 1
| [we]](#manual-Weekday___we-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_) => 2
| [th]](#manual-Weekday___th-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_) => 3
| [fr]](#manual-Weekday___fr-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_) => 4
| [sa]](#manual-Weekday___sa-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_) => 5
| [su]](#manual-Weekday___su-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_) => 6
def Weekday.fromFin : [Fin](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Finite-Natural-Numbers/#Fin___mk) 7 → [Weekday]](#manual-Weekday-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_)
| 0 => [mo]](#manual-Weekday___mo-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_)
| 1 => [tu]](#manual-Weekday___tu-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_)
| 2 => [we]](#manual-Weekday___we-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_)
| 3 => [th]](#manual-Weekday___th-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_)
| 4 => [fr]](#manual-Weekday___fr-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_)
| 5 => [sa]](#manual-Weekday___sa-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_)
| 6 => [su]](#manual-Weekday___su-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_)
```

Each type can be coerced to the other:

```lean
instance : [Coe]](#manual-Coe___mk) [Weekday]](#manual-Weekday-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_) ([Fin](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Finite-Natural-Numbers/#Fin___mk) 7) where
[coe]](#manual-Coe___mk) := [Weekday.toFin]](#manual-Weekday___toFin-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_)
instance : [Coe]](#manual-Coe___mk) ([Fin](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Finite-Natural-Numbers/#Fin___mk) 7) [Weekday]](#manual-Weekday-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_) where
[coe]](#manual-Coe___mk) := [Weekday.fromFin]](#manual-Weekday___fromFin-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_)
```

While this works, instances of the coercions that occur in Lean's output are not presented using the coercion operator, which is what Lean users expect.
Instead, the name `[Weekday.fromFin]](#manual-Weekday___fromFin-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_)` is used explicitly:

```lean
def wednesday : [Weekday]](#manual-Weekday-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_) := (2 : [Fin](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Finite-Natural-Numbers/#Fin___mk) 7)
#print [wednesday]](#manual-wednesday-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_)
```

```lean
def wednesday : [Weekday]](#manual-Weekday-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_) :=
[Weekday.fromFin]](#manual-Weekday___fromFin-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_) 2
```

Adding the `coe` attribute to the definition of a coercion causes it to be displayed using the coercion operator:

```lean
[attribute]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___attribute) [[coe]](#manual-Lean___Attr___coe)] [Weekday.fromFin]](#manual-Weekday___fromFin-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_)
[attribute]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___attribute) [[coe]](#manual-Lean___Attr___coe)] [Weekday.toFin]](#manual-Weekday___toFin-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_)
def friday : [Weekday]](#manual-Weekday-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_) := (5 : [Fin](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Finite-Natural-Numbers/#Fin___mk) 7)
#print [friday]](#manual-friday-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_)
```

```lean
def friday : [Weekday]](#manual-Weekday-_LPAR_in-Implementing-Coercions_RPAR_) :=
↑5
```

### 11.2.2. Coercions from Natural Numbers and Integers {#manual-nat-api-cast}

The type classes `[NatCast]](#manual-NatCast___mk)` and `[IntCast]](#manual-IntCast___mk)` are special cases of `[Coe]](#manual-Coe___mk)` that are used to define a coercion from `[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)` or `[Int](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Integers/#Int___ofNat)` to some other type that is in some sense canonical.
They exist to enable better integration with large libraries of mathematics, such as [Mathlib](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4), that make heavy use of coercions to map from the natural numbers or integers to other structures (typically rings).
Ideally, the coercion of a natural number or integer into these structures is a [simp normal form](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/The-Simplifier/Simp-Normal-Forms/#--tech-term-simp-normal-form), because it is a convenient way to denote them.

When the coercion application is expected to be the [simp normal form](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/The-Simplifier/Simp-Normal-Forms/#--tech-term-simp-normal-form) for a type, it is important that *all* such coercions are [definitionally equal]](#manual---tech-term-definitional-equality) in practice.
Otherwise, the [simp normal form](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/The-Simplifier/Simp-Normal-Forms/#--tech-term-simp-normal-form) would need to choose a single chained coercion path, but lemmas could accidentally be stated using a different path.
Because `[simp](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#simp)`'s internal index is based on the underlying structure of the term, rather than its presentation in the surface syntax, these differences would cause the lemmas to not be applied where expected.
`[NatCast]](#manual-NatCast___mk)` and `[IntCast]](#manual-IntCast___mk)` instances, on the other hand, should be defined such that they are always [definitionally equal]](#manual---tech-term-definitional-equality), avoiding the problem.
The Lean standard library's instances are arranged such that `[NatCast]](#manual-NatCast___mk)` or `[IntCast]](#manual-IntCast___mk)` instances are chosen preferentially over chains of coercion instances during coercion insertion.
They can also be used as `[CoeOut]](#manual-CoeOut___mk)` instances, allowing a graceful fallback to coercion chaining when needed.

type class

```lean
[NatCast.{u}]](#manual-NatCast___mk) (R : Type u) : Type u



[NatCast.{u}]](#manual-NatCast___mk) (R : Type u) : Type u
```

The canonical homomorphism `[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → R`. In most use cases, the target type will have a (semi)ring
structure, and this homomorphism should be a (semi)ring homomorphism.

`[NatCast]](#manual-NatCast___mk)` and `[IntCast]](#manual-IntCast___mk)` exist to allow different libraries with their own types that can be notated
as natural numbers to have consistent `[simp](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#simp)` normal forms without needing to create coercion
simplification sets that are aware of all combinations. Libraries should make it easy to work with
`[NatCast]](#manual-NatCast___mk)` where possible. For instance, in Mathlib there will be such a homomorphism (and thus a
`[NatCast]](#manual-NatCast___mk) R` instance) whenever `R` is an additive monoid with a `1`.

The prototypical example is `[Int.ofNat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Integers/#Int___ofNat)`.



The canonical map `[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → R`.

def

```lean

[Nat.cast.{u}]](#manual-Nat___cast) {R : Type u} [[NatCast]](#manual-NatCast___mk) R] :
  [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → R
```

The canonical homomorphism `[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) → R`. In most use cases, the target type will have a (semi)ring
structure, and this homomorphism should be a (semi)ring homomorphism.

`[NatCast]](#manual-NatCast___mk)` and `[IntCast]](#manual-IntCast___mk)` exist to allow different libraries with their own types that can be notated
as natural numbers to have consistent `[simp](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#simp)` normal forms without needing to create coercion
simplification sets that are aware of all combinations. Libraries should make it easy to work with
`[NatCast]](#manual-NatCast___mk)` where possible. For instance, in Mathlib there will be such a homomorphism (and thus a
`[NatCast]](#manual-NatCast___mk) R` instance) whenever `R` is an additive monoid with a `1`.

The prototypical example is `[Int.ofNat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Integers/#Int___ofNat)`.

```lean
[IntCast.{u}]](#manual-IntCast___mk) (R : Type u) : Type u
```

The canonical homomorphism `[Int](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Integers/#Int___ofNat) → R`. In most use cases, the target type will have a ring structure,

## Coercions — 11.3. Coercing to Sorts {#manual-coercions-113-coercing-to-sorts}

> 📄 Source: https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Coercions/Coercing-to-Sorts/

The Lean elaborator expects types in certain positions without necessarily being able to determine the type's [universe]](#manual---tech-term-universes) ahead of time.
For example, the term following the colon in a definition header might be a proposition or a type.
The ordinary coercion mechanism is not applicable because it requires a specific expected type, and there's no way to express that the expected type could be *any* universe in the `[Coe]](#manual-Coe___mk)` class.

When a term is elaborated in a position where a proposition or type is expected, but the inferred type of the elaborated term is not a proposition or type, Lean attempts to recover from the error by synthesizing an instance of `[CoeSort]](#manual-CoeSort___mk)`.
If the instance is found, and the resulting type is itself a type, then it the coercion is inserted and unfolded.

Not every situation in which the elaborator expects a universe requires `[CoeSort]](#manual-CoeSort___mk)`.
In some cases, a particular universe is available as an expected type.
In these situations, ordinary coercion insertion using `[CoeT]](#manual-CoeT___mk)` is used.
Instances of `[CoeSort]](#manual-CoeSort___mk)` can be used to synthesize instances of `[CoeOut]](#manual-CoeOut___mk)`, so no separate instance is needed to support this use case.
In general, coercions to types should be implemented as `[CoeSort]](#manual-CoeSort___mk)`.

type class

```lean
[CoeSort.{u, v}]](#manual-CoeSort___mk) (α : Sort u) (β : [outParam]](#manual-outParam) (Sort v)) :
  Sort (max (max 1 u) v)



[CoeSort.{u, v}]](#manual-CoeSort___mk) (α : Sort u)
  (β : [outParam]](#manual-outParam) (Sort v)) :
  Sort (max (max 1 u) v)
```

`[CoeSort]](#manual-CoeSort___mk) α β` is a coercion to a sort. `β` must be a universe, and this is
triggered when `a : α` appears in a place where a type is expected, like
`(x : a)` or `a → a`.
`[CoeSort]](#manual-CoeSort___mk)` instances apply to `[CoeOut]](#manual-CoeOut___mk)` as well.

Instance Constructor

```lean
[CoeSort.mk]](#manual-CoeSort___mk).{u, v}
```

Methods

```lean
coe : α → β
```

Coerces a value of type `α` to `β`, which must be a universe.

syntaxExplicit Coercion to Sorts

```lean
term ::= ...
    | ↥ term
```

Coercions to sorts can be explicitly triggered using the `↥` prefix operator.

**Example: Sort Coercions**

A monoid is a type equipped with an associative binary operation and an identity element.
While monoid structure can be defined as a type class, it can also be defined as a structure that “bundles up” the structure with the type:

```lean
structure Monoid where
Carrier : Type u
op : Carrier → Carrier → Carrier
id : Carrier
op_assoc :
∀ (x y z : Carrier), op x (op y z) = op (op x y) z
id_op_identity : ∀ (x : Carrier), op id x = x
op_id_identity : ∀ (x : Carrier), op x id = x
```

The type `[Monoid]](#manual-Monoid-_LPAR_in-Sort-Coercions_RPAR_)` does not indicate the carrier:

```lean
def StringMonoid : [Monoid]](#manual-Monoid-_LPAR_in-Sort-Coercions_RPAR_) where
[Carrier]](#manual-Monoid___Carrier-_LPAR_in-Sort-Coercions_RPAR_) := [String](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Strings/#String___ofByteArray)
[op]](#manual-Monoid___op-_LPAR_in-Sort-Coercions_RPAR_) := (· ++ ·)
[id]](#manual-Monoid___id-_LPAR_in-Sort-Coercions_RPAR_) := ""
[op_assoc]](#manual-Monoid___op_assoc-_LPAR_in-Sort-Coercions_RPAR_) := by⊢ ∀ (x y z : [String](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Strings/#String___ofByteArray)), x [++]](#manual-HAppend___mk) [(]](#manual-HAppend___mk)y [++]](#manual-HAppend___mk) z[)]](#manual-HAppend___mk) [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) x [++]](#manual-HAppend___mk) y [++]](#manual-HAppend___mk) z [intros](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#intros)x✝:[String](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Strings/#String___ofByteArray)y✝:[String](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Strings/#String___ofByteArray)z✝:[String](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Strings/#String___ofByteArray)⊢ x✝ [++]](#manual-HAppend___mk) [(]](#manual-HAppend___mk)y✝ [++]](#manual-HAppend___mk) z✝[)]](#manual-HAppend___mk) [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) x✝ [++]](#manual-HAppend___mk) y✝ [++]](#manual-HAppend___mk) z✝; [simp](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#simp) [String.append_assoc]All goals completed! 🐙
[id_op_identity]](#manual-Monoid___id_op_identity-_LPAR_in-Sort-Coercions_RPAR_) := by⊢ ∀ (x : [String](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Strings/#String___ofByteArray)), "" [++]](#manual-HAppend___mk) x [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) x [intros](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#intros)x✝:[String](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Strings/#String___ofByteArray)⊢ "" [++]](#manual-HAppend___mk) x✝ [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) x✝; [simp](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#simp)All goals completed! 🐙
[op_id_identity]](#manual-Monoid___op_id_identity-_LPAR_in-Sort-Coercions_RPAR_) := by⊢ ∀ (x : [String](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Strings/#String___ofByteArray)), x [++]](#manual-HAppend___mk) "" [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) x [intros](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#intros)x✝:[String](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Strings/#String___ofByteArray)⊢ x✝ [++]](#manual-HAppend___mk) "" [=](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Propositions/Propositional-Equality/#Eq___refl) x✝; [simp](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#simp)All goals completed! 🐙
```

However, a `[CoeSort]](#manual-CoeSort___mk)` instance can be implemented that applies the `[Monoid.Carrier]](#manual-Monoid___Carrier-_LPAR_in-Sort-Coercions_RPAR_)` projection when a monoid is used in a position where Lean would expect a type:

```lean
instance : [CoeSort]](#manual-CoeSort___mk) [Monoid]](#manual-Monoid-_LPAR_in-Sort-Coercions_RPAR_) (Type u) where
[coe]](#manual-CoeSort___mk) m := m.[Carrier]](#manual-Monoid___Carrier-_LPAR_in-Sort-Coercions_RPAR_)
example : [StringMonoid]](#manual-StringMonoid-_LPAR_in-Sort-Coercions_RPAR_) := "hello"
```

**Example: Sort Coercions as Ordinary Coercions**

The [inductive type]](#manual---tech-term-Inductive-types) `[NatOrBool]](#manual-NatOrBool-_LPAR_in-Sort-Coercions-as-Ordinary-Coercions_RPAR_)` represents the types `[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)` and `[Bool](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Booleans/#Bool___false)`.
They can be coerced to the actual types `[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)` and `[Bool](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Booleans/#Bool___false)`:

```lean
inductive NatOrBool where
| nat | bool
@[[coe]](#manual-Lean___Attr___coe)]
abbrev NatOrBool.asType : [NatOrBool]](#manual-NatOrBool-_LPAR_in-Sort-Coercions-as-Ordinary-Coercions_RPAR_) → Type
| [.nat]](#manual-NatOrBool___nat-_LPAR_in-Sort-Coercions-as-Ordinary-Coercions_RPAR_) => [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)
| [.bool]](#manual-NatOrBool___bool-_LPAR_in-Sort-Coercions-as-Ordinary-Coercions_RPAR_) => [Bool](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Booleans/#Bool___false)
instance : [CoeSort]](#manual-CoeSort___mk) [NatOrBool]](#manual-NatOrBool-_LPAR_in-Sort-Coercions-as-Ordinary-Coercions_RPAR_) Type where
[coe]](#manual-CoeSort___mk) := [NatOrBool.asType]](#manual-NatOrBool___asType-_LPAR_in-Sort-Coercions-as-Ordinary-Coercions_RPAR_)
[open]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___open) NatOrBool
```

The `[CoeSort]](#manual-CoeSort___mk)` instance is used when `[nat]](#manual-NatOrBool___nat-_LPAR_in-Sort-Coercions-as-Ordinary-Coercions_RPAR_)` occurs to the right of a colon:

```lean
def x : [nat]](#manual-NatOrBool___nat-_LPAR_in-Sort-Coercions-as-Ordinary-Coercions_RPAR_) := 5
```

When an expected type is available, ordinary coercion insertion is used.
In this case, the `[CoeSort]](#manual-CoeSort___mk)` instance is used to synthesize a `[CoeOut]](#manual-CoeOut___mk) [NatOrBool]](#manual-NatOrBool-_LPAR_in-Sort-Coercions-as-Ordinary-Coercions_RPAR_) Type` instance, which chains with the `[Coe]](#manual-Coe___mk) Type ([Option](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Optional-Values/#Option___none) Type)` instance to recover from the type error.

```lean
def y : [Option](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Optional-Values/#Option___none) Type := [bool]](#manual-NatOrBool___bool-_LPAR_in-Sort-Coercions-as-Ordinary-Coercions_RPAR_)
```

## Coercions — 11.4. Coercing to Function Types {#manual-coercions-114-coercing-to-function-types}

> 📄 Source: https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Coercions/Coercing-to-Function-Types/

Another situation where an expected type is not generally available is the function position in a function application term.
Dependent function types are common; together with [implicit](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Terms/Functions/#--tech-term-implicit) parameters, they cause information to flow from the elaboration of one argument to the elaboration of the others.
Attempting to deduce the type required for the function from the expected type of the entire application term and individually-inferred types of arguments will often fail.
In these situations, Lean uses the `[CoeFun]](#manual-CoeFun___mk)` type class to coerce a non-function in an application position into a function.
Like `[CoeSort]](#manual-CoeSort___mk)`, `[CoeFun]](#manual-CoeFun___mk)` instances do not chain with other coercions while inserting a function coercion, but they can be used as `[CoeOut]](#manual-CoeOut___mk)` instances during ordinary coercion insertion.

The second parameter to `[CoeFun]](#manual-CoeFun___mk)` is an output parameter that determines the resulting function type.
This output parameter is function that computes the function type from the term that's being coerced, rather than the function type itself.
Unlike `[CoeDep]](#manual-CoeDep___mk)`, the term itself is not taken into account during instance synthesis; it can, however, be used to create dependently typed coercions where the function type is determined by the term.

type class

```lean
[CoeFun.{u, v}]](#manual-CoeFun___mk) (α : Sort u) (γ : [outParam]](#manual-outParam) (α → Sort v)) :
  Sort (max (max 1 u) v)



[CoeFun.{u, v}]](#manual-CoeFun___mk) (α : Sort u)
  (γ : [outParam]](#manual-outParam) (α → Sort v)) :
  Sort (max (max 1 u) v)
```

`[CoeFun]](#manual-CoeFun___mk) α (γ : α → Sort v)` is a coercion to a function. `γ a` should be a
(coercion-to-)function type, and this is triggered whenever an element
`f : α` appears in an application like `f x`, which would not make sense since
`f` does not have a function type.
`[CoeFun]](#manual-CoeFun___mk)` instances apply to `[CoeOut]](#manual-CoeOut___mk)` as well.

Instance Constructor

```lean
[CoeFun.mk]](#manual-CoeFun___mk).{u, v}
```

Methods

```lean
coe : (f : α) → γ f
```

Coerces a value `f : α` to type `γ f`, which should be either be a
function type or another `[CoeFun]](#manual-CoeFun___mk)` type, in order to resolve a mistyped
application `f x`.

syntaxExplicit Coercion to Functions

```lean
term ::= ...
    | ⇑ term
```

**Example: Coercing Decorated Functions to Function Types**

The structure `[NamedFun]](#manual-NamedFun-_LPAR_in-Coercing-Decorated-Functions-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) α β` pairs a function from `α` to `β` with a name.

```lean
structure NamedFun (α : Type u) (β : Type v) where
function : α → β
name : [String](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Strings/#String___ofByteArray)
```

Existing functions can be named:

```lean
def succ : [NamedFun]](#manual-NamedFun-_LPAR_in-Coercing-Decorated-Functions-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero) where
[function]](#manual-NamedFun___function-_LPAR_in-Coercing-Decorated-Functions-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) n := n + 1
[name]](#manual-NamedFun___name-_LPAR_in-Coercing-Decorated-Functions-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) := "succ"
def asString [ToString α] : [NamedFun]](#manual-NamedFun-_LPAR_in-Coercing-Decorated-Functions-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) α [String](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Strings/#String___ofByteArray) where
[function]](#manual-NamedFun___function-_LPAR_in-Coercing-Decorated-Functions-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) := ToString.toString
[name]](#manual-NamedFun___name-_LPAR_in-Coercing-Decorated-Functions-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) := "asString"
def append : [NamedFun]](#manual-NamedFun-_LPAR_in-Coercing-Decorated-Functions-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) ([List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) α) ([List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) α → [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) α) where
[function]](#manual-NamedFun___function-_LPAR_in-Coercing-Decorated-Functions-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) := (· ++ ·)
[name]](#manual-NamedFun___name-_LPAR_in-Coercing-Decorated-Functions-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) := "append"
```

Named functions can also be composed:

```lean
def NamedFun.comp
(f : [NamedFun]](#manual-NamedFun-_LPAR_in-Coercing-Decorated-Functions-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) β γ)
(g : [NamedFun]](#manual-NamedFun-_LPAR_in-Coercing-Decorated-Functions-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) α β) :
[NamedFun]](#manual-NamedFun-_LPAR_in-Coercing-Decorated-Functions-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) α γ where
[function]](#manual-NamedFun___function-_LPAR_in-Coercing-Decorated-Functions-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) := f.[function]](#manual-NamedFun___function-_LPAR_in-Coercing-Decorated-Functions-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) ∘ g.[function]](#manual-NamedFun___function-_LPAR_in-Coercing-Decorated-Functions-to-Function-Types_RPAR_)
[name]](#manual-NamedFun___name-_LPAR_in-Coercing-Decorated-Functions-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) := f.[name]](#manual-NamedFun___name-_LPAR_in-Coercing-Decorated-Functions-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) ++ " ∘ " ++ g.[name]](#manual-NamedFun___name-_LPAR_in-Coercing-Decorated-Functions-to-Function-Types_RPAR_)
```

Unlike ordinary functions, named functions have a reasonable representation as a string:

```lean
instance : ToString ([NamedFun]](#manual-NamedFun-_LPAR_in-Coercing-Decorated-Functions-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) α α'') where
toString f := s!"#<{f.[name]](#manual-NamedFun___name-_LPAR_in-Coercing-Decorated-Functions-to-Function-Types_RPAR_)}>"
```

```lean
[#eval]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___eval) [asString]](#manual-asString-_LPAR_in-Coercing-Decorated-Functions-to-Function-Types_RPAR_).[comp]](#manual-NamedFun___comp-_LPAR_in-Coercing-Decorated-Functions-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) [succ]](#manual-succ-_LPAR_in-Coercing-Decorated-Functions-to-Function-Types_RPAR_)
```

```lean
#<asString ∘ succ>
```

A `[CoeFun]](#manual-CoeFun___mk)` instance allows them to be applied just like ordinary functions:

```lean
instance : [CoeFun]](#manual-CoeFun___mk) ([NamedFun]](#manual-NamedFun-_LPAR_in-Coercing-Decorated-Functions-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) α α'') (fun _ => α → α'') where
[coe]](#manual-CoeFun___mk) | ⟨f, _⟩ => f
```

```lean
[#eval]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___eval) [append]](#manual-append-_LPAR_in-Coercing-Decorated-Functions-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) [1, 2, 3] [4, 5, 6]
```

```lean
[[](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil)1[,](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) 2[,](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) 3[,](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) 4[,](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) 5[,](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) 6[]](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil)
```

**Example: Dependent Coercion to Functions**

Sometimes, the type of the resulting function depends on the specific value that is being coerced.
A `[Writer]](#manual-Writer-_LPAR_in-Dependent-Coercion-to-Functions_RPAR_)` represents a means of appending a representation of some value to a string:

```lean
structure Writer where
Writes : Type u
write : Writes → [String](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Strings/#String___ofByteArray) → [String](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Strings/#String___ofByteArray)
def natWriter : [Writer]](#manual-Writer-_LPAR_in-Dependent-Coercion-to-Functions_RPAR_) where
[Writes]](#manual-Writer___Writes-_LPAR_in-Dependent-Coercion-to-Functions_RPAR_) := [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)
[write]](#manual-Writer___write-_LPAR_in-Dependent-Coercion-to-Functions_RPAR_) n out := out ++ toString n
def stringWriter : [Writer]](#manual-Writer-_LPAR_in-Dependent-Coercion-to-Functions_RPAR_) where
[Writes]](#manual-Writer___Writes-_LPAR_in-Dependent-Coercion-to-Functions_RPAR_) := [String](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Strings/#String___ofByteArray)
[write]](#manual-Writer___write-_LPAR_in-Dependent-Coercion-to-Functions_RPAR_) s out := out ++ s
```

Because the type of the parameter expected by the inner function depend on the `[Writer.Writes]](#manual-Writer___Writes-_LPAR_in-Dependent-Coercion-to-Functions_RPAR_)` field, the `[CoeFun]](#manual-CoeFun___mk)` instance extracts the field:

```lean
instance :
[CoeFun]](#manual-CoeFun___mk) [Writer]](#manual-Writer-_LPAR_in-Dependent-Coercion-to-Functions_RPAR_) (·.[Writes]](#manual-Writer___Writes-_LPAR_in-Dependent-Coercion-to-Functions_RPAR_) → [String](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Strings/#String___ofByteArray) → [String](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Strings/#String___ofByteArray)) where
[coe]](#manual-CoeFun___mk) w := w.[write]](#manual-Writer___write-_LPAR_in-Dependent-Coercion-to-Functions_RPAR_)
```

With this instance, concrete `[Writer]](#manual-Writer-_LPAR_in-Dependent-Coercion-to-Functions_RPAR_)`s can be used as functions:

```lean
[#eval]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___eval) "" |> [natWriter]](#manual-natWriter-_LPAR_in-Dependent-Coercion-to-Functions_RPAR_) (5 : [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)) |> [stringWriter]](#manual-stringWriter-_LPAR_in-Dependent-Coercion-to-Functions_RPAR_) " hello"
```

```lean
"5 hello"
```

**Example: Coercing to Function Types**

A well-typed interpreter is an interpreter for a programming language that uses indexed families to rule out run-time type errors.
Functions written in the interpreted language can be interpreted as Lean functions, but their underlying source code can also be inspected.

The first step in the well-typed interpreter is to select the subset of Lean types that can be used.
These types are represented by an [inductive type]](#manual---tech-term-Inductive-types) of codes `[Ty]](#manual-Ty-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_)` and a function that maps these codes to actual types.

```lean
inductive Ty where
| nat
| arr (dom cod : [Ty]](#manual-Ty-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_))
abbrev Ty.interp : [Ty]](#manual-Ty-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) → Type
| [.nat]](#manual-Ty___nat-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) => [Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)
| [.arr]](#manual-Ty___arr-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) t t' => t.[interp]](#manual-Ty___interp-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) → t'.[interp]](#manual-Ty___interp-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_)
```

The language itself is represented by an [indexed family]](#manual---tech-term-indexed-families) over variable contexts and result types.
Variables are represented by [de Bruijn indices](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Bruijn_index).

```lean
inductive Tm : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) [Ty]](#manual-Ty-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) → [Ty]](#manual-Ty-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) → Type where
| zero : [Tm]](#manual-Tm-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) Γ [.nat]](#manual-Ty___nat-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_)
| succ (n : [Tm]](#manual-Tm-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) Γ [.nat]](#manual-Ty___nat-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_)) : [Tm]](#manual-Tm-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) Γ [.nat]](#manual-Ty___nat-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_)
| rep (n : [Tm]](#manual-Tm-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) Γ [.nat]](#manual-Ty___nat-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_))
(start : [Tm]](#manual-Tm-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) Γ t)
(f : [Tm]](#manual-Tm-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) Γ ([.arr]](#manual-Ty___arr-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) [.nat]](#manual-Ty___nat-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) ([.arr]](#manual-Ty___arr-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) t t))) :
[Tm]](#manual-Tm-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) Γ t
| lam (body : [Tm]](#manual-Tm-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) (t :: Γ) t') : [Tm]](#manual-Tm-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) Γ ([.arr]](#manual-Ty___arr-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) t t')
| app (f : [Tm]](#manual-Tm-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) Γ ([.arr]](#manual-Ty___arr-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) t t')) (arg : [Tm]](#manual-Tm-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) Γ t) : [Tm]](#manual-Tm-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) Γ t'
| var (i : [Fin](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Finite-Natural-Numbers/#Fin___mk) Γ.[length](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___length)) : [Tm]](#manual-Tm-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) Γ Γ[i]
[deriving]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___optDeriving-next) [Repr]](#manual-Repr___mk)
```

Because the `[OfNat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Terms/Numeric-Literals/#OfNat___mk)` instance for `[Fin](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Finite-Natural-Numbers/#Fin___mk)` requires that the upper bound be non-zero, `[Tm.var]](#manual-Tm___var-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_)` can be inconvenient to use with numeric literals.
The helper `[Tm.v]](#manual-Tm___v-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_)` can be used to avoid the need for type annotations in these cases.

```lean
def Tm.v
(i : [Fin](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Finite-Natural-Numbers/#Fin___mk) (Γ.[length](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___length) + 1)) :
[Tm]](#manual-Tm-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) (t :: Γ) (t :: Γ)[i] :=
[.var]](#manual-Tm___var-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) (Γ := t :: Γ) i
```

A function that adds two natural numbers uses the `[rep]](#manual-Tm___rep-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_)` operation to apply the successor `[Tm.succ]](#manual-Tm___succ-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_)` repeatedly.

```lean
def plus : [Tm]](#manual-Tm-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) [] ([.arr]](#manual-Ty___arr-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) [.nat]](#manual-Ty___nat-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) ([.arr]](#manual-Ty___arr-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) [.nat]](#manual-Ty___nat-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) [.nat]](#manual-Ty___nat-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_))) :=
[.lam]](#manual-Tm___lam-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) <| [.lam]](#manual-Tm___lam-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) <| [.rep]](#manual-Tm___rep-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) ([.v]](#manual-Tm___v-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) 1) ([.v]](#manual-Tm___v-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) 0) ([.lam]](#manual-Tm___lam-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) ([.lam]](#manual-Tm___lam-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) ([.succ]](#manual-Tm___succ-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) ([.v]](#manual-Tm___v-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) 0))))
```

Each typing context can be interpreted as a type of run-time environments that provide a value for each variable in the context:

```lean
def Env : [List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) [Ty]](#manual-Ty-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) → Type
| [] => [Unit](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/The-Unit-Type/#Unit)
| t :: Γ => t.[interp]](#manual-Ty___interp-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) × [Env]](#manual-Env-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) Γ
def Env.empty : [Env]](#manual-Env-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) [] := ()
def Env.extend (ρ : [Env]](#manual-Env-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) Γ) (v : t.[interp]](#manual-Ty___interp-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_)) : [Env]](#manual-Env-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) (t :: Γ) :=
(v, ρ)
def Env.get (i : [Fin](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Finite-Natural-Numbers/#Fin___mk) Γ.[length](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___length)) (ρ : [Env]](#manual-Env-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) Γ) : Γ[i].[interp]](#manual-Ty___interp-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) :=
[match](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Terms/Pattern-Matching/#Lean___Parser___Term___match) Γ, ρ, i [with](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Terms/Pattern-Matching/#Lean___Parser___Term___match)
| _::_, (v, _), ⟨0, _⟩ => v
| _::_, (_, ρ'), ⟨i+1, _⟩ => ρ'.[get]](#manual-Env___get-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) ⟨i, byΓ:[List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) [Ty]](#manual-Ty-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_)i✝:[Fin](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Finite-Natural-Numbers/#Fin___mk) Γ.[length](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___length)ρ:[Env]](#manual-Env-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) Γhead✝:[Ty]](#manual-Ty-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_)tail✝:[List](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) [Ty]](#manual-Ty-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_)fst✝:head✝.[interp]](#manual-Ty___interp-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_)ρ':[Env]](#manual-Env-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) tail✝i:[Nat](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___zero)isLt✝:i [+]](#manual-HAdd___mk) 1 [<]](#manual-LT___mk) [(](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil)head✝ [::](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil) tail✝[)](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___nil).[length](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___length)⊢ i [<]](#manual-LT___mk) tail✝.[length](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Linked-Lists/#List___length) [simp_all](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Tactic-Proofs/Tactic-Reference/#simp_all)All goals completed! 🐙⟩
```

Finally, the interpreter is a recursive function over the term:

```lean
def Tm.interp (ρ : [Env]](#manual-Env-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) α'') : [Tm]](#manual-Tm-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) α'' t → t.[interp]](#manual-Ty___interp-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_)
| [.zero]](#manual-Tm___zero-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) => 0
| [.succ]](#manual-Tm___succ-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) n => n.[interp]](#manual-Tm___interp-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) ρ + 1
| [.rep]](#manual-Tm___rep-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) n start f =>
let f' := f.[interp]](#manual-Tm___interp-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) ρ
(n.[interp]](#manual-Tm___interp-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) ρ).[fold](https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Basic-Types/Natural-Numbers/#Nat___fold) (fun n _ x => f' n x) (start.[interp]](#manual-Tm___interp-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) ρ)
| [.lam]](#manual-Tm___lam-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) body => fun x => body.[interp]](#manual-Tm___interp-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) (ρ.[extend]](#manual-Env___extend-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) x)
| [.app]](#manual-Tm___app-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) f arg => f.[interp]](#manual-Tm___interp-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) ρ (arg.[interp]](#manual-Tm___interp-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) ρ)
| [.var]](#manual-Tm___var-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) i => ρ.[get]](#manual-Env___get-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) i
```

Coercing a `[Tm]](#manual-Tm-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_)` to a function consists of calling the interpreter.

```lean
instance : [CoeFun]](#manual-CoeFun___mk) ([Tm]](#manual-Tm-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) [] α'') (fun _ => α''.[interp]](#manual-Ty___interp-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_)) where
[coe]](#manual-CoeFun___mk) f := f.[interp]](#manual-Tm___interp-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) [.empty]](#manual-Env___empty-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_)
```

Because functions are represented by a first-order inductive type, their code can be inspected:

```lean
[#eval]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___eval) [plus]](#manual-plus-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_)
```

```lean
Tm.lam (Tm.lam (Tm.rep (Tm.var 1) (Tm.var 0) (Tm.lam (Tm.lam (Tm.succ (Tm.var 0))))))
```

At the same time, due to the coercion, they can be applied just like native Lean functions:

```lean
[#eval]](#manual-Lean___Parser___Command___eval) [plus]](#manual-plus-_LPAR_in-Coercing-to-Function-Types_RPAR_) 3 5
```

```lean
8
```

## Coercions — 11.5. Implementation Details {#manual-coercions-115-implementation-details}

> 📄 Source: https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/Coercions/Implementation-Details/

Only ordinary coercion insertion uses chaining.
Inserting coercions to a [sort]](#manual-sort-coercion) or a [function]](#manual-fun-coercion) uses ordinary instance synthesis.
Similarly, [dependent coercions]](#manual---tech-term-Dependent-coercions) are not chained.

### 11.5.1. Unfolding Coercions {#manual-coercion-unfold-impl}

The coercion insertion mechanism unfolds applications of coercions, which allows them to control the specific shape of the resulting term.
This is important both to ensure readable proof goals and to control evaluation of the coerced term in compiled code.
Unfolding coercions is controlled by the `coe_decl` attribute, which is applied to each coercion method (e.g. `[Coe.coe]](#manual-Coe___mk)`).
This attribute should be considered part of the internals of the coercion mechanism, rather than part of the public coercion API.

### 11.5.2. Coercion Chaining {#manual-coercion-chain-impl}

Coercion chaining is implemented through a collection of auxiliary type classes.
Users should not write instances of these classes directly, but knowledge of their structure can be useful when diagnosing the reason why a coercion was not inserted as expected.
The specific rules governing the ordering of instances in the chain (namely, that it should match `[CoeHead]](#manual-CoeHead___mk)`﻿`?``[CoeOut]](#manual-CoeOut___mk)`﻿`*``[Coe]](#manual-Coe___mk)`﻿`*``[CoeTail]](#manual-CoeTail___mk)`﻿`?`) are implemented by the following type classes:

- `[CoeTC]](#manual-CoeTC___mk)` is the transitive closure of `[Coe]](#manual-Coe___mk)` instances.
- `[CoeOTC]](#manual-CoeOTC___mk)` is the middle of the chain, consisting of the transitive closure of `[CoeOut]](#manual-CoeOut___mk)` instances followed by `[CoeTC]](#manual-CoeTC___mk)`.
- `[CoeHTC]](#manual-CoeHTC___mk)` is the start of the chain, consisting of at most one `[CoeHead]](#manual-CoeHead___mk)` instance followed by `[CoeOTC]](#manual-CoeOTC___mk)`.
- `[CoeHTCT]](#manual-CoeHTCT___mk)` is the whole chain, consisting of `CoeHTC` followed by at most one `[CoeTail]](#manual-CoeTail___mk)` instance. Alternatively, it might be a `[NatCast]](#manual-NatCast___mk)` instance.
- `[CoeT]](#manual-CoeT___mk)` represents the entire chain: it is either a `[CoeHTCT]](#manual-CoeHTCT___mk)` chain or a single `[CoeDep]](#manual-CoeDep___mk)` instance.

type class
